properties.decision: Anthony, 2026-09-05: yes. This REVERSES dec:read-hint-shape option C for the loop-DEBT half of the read-side hint. service.rs:3731 read_loop_hint computed g.loop_status() on the first read after every write (cache keyed on write_gen, bumped on every write-lock). Measured: 7.7 s per write-to-read boundary on a scratch store, ~12 s on the live daemon, 9.5 boundaries per session across 61 real sessions - 1.2 to 1.9 minutes of unrequested rollup per session, decorating reads that cost 1-4 ms. The loop already speaks in two places - the loop_status tool every session is instructed to run, and the Stop hook. WHAT IS KEPT, and why this is not a full reversal: the same function also carries record_moved - the notice that a colleague's export landed - which Anthony chose on 2026-08-13 to ride on ordinary reads precisely so a session learns it without thinking to ask (cap:the-record-moved-reaches-an-ordinary-read). That half stays, gated on generation as today; its cost is the sync read, which dec:an-unchanged-sync-target-is-not-re-parsed makes near zero. cap:read-loop-hint narrows to record_moved only. The write-side static loop_hint sentence is untouched.
properties.name: DECIDED - reads no longer recompute loop_status for a hint; the loop speaks when loop_status is called. record_moved stays on reads.
properties.rationale: Chosen over computing the debt hint asynchronously or from incremental counters because it is the smallest change that meets con:a-read-after-a-write-costs-at-most-twice-the-same-read-warm outright and removes work rather than doing it faster. The record_moved half is kept because it is a different feature with its own capability and its own ruling, and removing it would silently undo a choice the measurement gave no reason to revisit.
